blocks.text: PRD: Harbor & Oak gift cards, in-store and online

This is the working cut for HBR-PRD-2022-034 on June 9, 2022. Dana Whitlock asked for a written bound after the current path (Paper cards in the drawer, no online redeem) stopped being honest. I am Michael Gilfilian, Web Developer, writing for Dana Whitlock, Jenna Park, and Nia Brooks. Primary host gift.harbor.internal. If you are skimming, jump the decision callout, then the refuse on Cartloom second ledger, then open questions. If you are implementing next week, jump the constraints, the numbers table, and the commands or contracts.

Shopify gift cards as the balance. POS sells them. Online redeems them. Reject Cartloom balance app ($129/mo, a second ledger). I am not restating a hallway yes. Cartloom second ledger is out because Two ledgers is how a $25 card becomes $0 online and $25 in the drawer. Dana will not explain that to a cousin. Cost of doing nothing is already in the numbers: look at mo=129, paper=200, avg=37.50, weeks=5, stores=1, cousin=1, ledger=1, fees=2.9. Sibling tickets HBR-2910 and HBR-TDD-2022-028. I will not reopen Cartloom second ledger in a side thread because a vendor sent a discount. Jenna Park is the acceptor unless the owners line says otherwise.
Decision for leadership

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: Shopify gift cards as the balance. POS sells them. Online redeems them. Reject Cartloom balance app ($129/mo, a second ledger).

Background on gift.harbor.internal. Paper cards in the drawer, no online redeem. That is the system Dana Whitlock lives with, not a slide. I timed or pulled the leftover on shop.harbor.internal the week before this file. Lag, stale minutes, or miss counts in this file are from that pull, not a round number I liked. Ticket HBR-PRD-2022-034 names the pull. If those numbers moved after June 9, 2022, update this file in review, do not 'correct' them in Slack.

blocks.text: Background. Why the current path is the wrong tool

Nia Brooks owns a leftover that is easy to skip: pos.harbor.internal. I will ping once. After that the owner is late, not blocked. Unique to this file (21): refuse on Cartloom second ledger, lock is one ledger, POS sell, online redeem, no third-party balance. I will not hide a product change inside a 'quick align' on HBR-2910.
If a card sold in the store does not work online, I will hear about it from a cousin on Sunday.

What a skeptical user would try first on gift.harbor.internal: the path Dana Whitlock actually has, not a desktop demo. Metric I will argue is time-to-useful, not a vanity QPS. If we cannot show that path on shop.harbor.internal with the numbers already in this file, we do not have a cut. Michael Gilfilian will not accept a laptop screenshot as that proof.

What I will not claim in HBR-PRD-2022-034

I will not claim Cartloom second ledger is impossible for a competitor. I will claim we will not buy it. I will not claim zero incidents after this cut. I will claim the next one dies at the gate named in the lock. Host gift.harbor.internal.
First useful slice for HBR-2910

First useful is one ledger, POS sell, online redeem, no third-party balance, not a prettier theme or a bigger box. Dana Whitlock sees that slice on gift.harbor.internal. If the slice needs a second product, that is a new ticket and Dana Whitlock is in the thread. I will not hide it inside HBR-PRD-2022-034.
